## Purpose and Entry Points
OpenMono is a local-first .NET 10 coding-agent runtime. Its primary executable is the CLI in `src/OpenMono.Cli/Program.cs`, launched by the `openmono` wrapper and installed through `get-openmono.sh`. It supports an interactive terminal agent, classic console mode, and an ACP server for VS Code/Cursor clients.

## Host Runtime and Conversation Control
`Program.cs` composes configuration, providers, tools, session state, rendering, and optional ACP hosting. The central agent control flow is `src/OpenMono.Cli/Session/ConversationLoop.cs`: user input becomes a model turn, model tool calls are dispatched, results are returned to the model, and the loop terminates on completion or safeguards. Session durability, resume, context accounting, compaction, checkpoints, artifacts, and tool-result caching are concentrated in `src/OpenMono.Cli/Session/SessionManager.cs`, `src/OpenMono.Cli/Session/Compactor.cs`, and `src/OpenMono.Cli/Session/Checkpointer.cs`.

## Model Provider Boundary
Provider-independent model calls pass through `src/OpenMono.Cli/Llm/ILlmClient.cs` and `src/OpenMono.Cli/Llm/ProviderRegistry.cs`. Implementations include local/OpenAI-compatible inference and Anthropic in `src/OpenMono.Cli/Llm/OpenAiCompatClient.cs` and `src/OpenMono.Cli/Llm/AnthropicClient.cs`. Local llama.cpp is the intended default runtime; external OpenAI, Anthropic, and Ollama-compatible endpoints are configurable alternatives. This boundary isolates agent orchestration from streaming/chat API formats and model selection.

## Tool Execution and Safety Boundary
The model cannot directly access the host: all actions use the tool registry and dispatcher in `src/OpenMono.Cli/Tools/ToolRegistry.cs` and `src/OpenMono.Cli/Tools/ToolDispatcher.cs`. Built-in file, patch, shell, search, web, LSP, Roslyn, memory, sub-agent, and playbook tools execute through `src/OpenMono.Cli/Tools/LocalToolExecutor.cs`. Calls are parsed and validated, subject to plan-mode policy and capability authorization, then cached/hooked/executed with artifacts recorded. Filesystem and capability containment are enforced by `src/OpenMono.Cli/Permissions/PermissionEngine.cs` and `src/OpenMono.Cli/Permissions/PathGuard.cs`; the Docker workspace mount is the operational blast-radius boundary.

## Interaction and ACP Service
Terminal interaction is rendered through the TUI/classic abstraction rooted in `src/OpenMono.Cli/Rendering/TerminalRenderer.cs` and `src/OpenMono.Cli/Rendering/AnsiTuiRenderer.cs`. ACP provides an alternate network-facing control plane: `src/OpenMono.Cli/Acp/AcpHostedService.cs` starts the service, `src/OpenMono.Cli/Acp/AcpServer.cs` exposes endpoints/session handling, and `src/OpenMono.Cli/Acp/AcpTurnRunner.cs` adapts ACP turns into the same conversation-loop machinery. This enables editor clients over the local ACP endpoint.

## Extensibility and Code Intelligence
MCP servers are managed and exposed as agent tools by `src/OpenMono.Cli/Mcp/McpServerManager.cs` and `src/OpenMono.Cli/Mcp/McpToolAdapter.cs`. Language intelligence is a separate process boundary via `src/OpenMono.Cli/Lsp/LspServerManager.cs`; Roslyn access is surfaced as a tool in `src/OpenMono.Cli/Tools/RoslynTool.cs`. YAML playbooks are loaded, parameterized, stateful, and executable through `src/OpenMono.Cli/Playbooks/PlaybookLoader.cs`, `src/OpenMono.Cli/Playbooks/PlaybookExecutor.cs`, and `src/OpenMono.Cli/Playbooks/PlaybookState.cs`.

## Deployment and External Services
Docker Compose provisions the agent/inference topology in `docker/docker-compose.yml`, with llama inference built from `docker/Dockerfile.llama` and agent containment from `docker/Dockerfile.agent`. Optional self-hosted web services include SearXNG (`docker/searxng/settings.yml`) and Scrapling/Camoufox (`docker/scrapling/app.py`), routed through Caddy (`docker/Caddyfile`). Setup scripts select CPU, NVIDIA, or Apple Silicon/Metal deployment paths; distributed inference can place the model runtime on another machine through tunnel setup.
